data.description:
## Problem

Removing the `refresh_scoped_snapshot(ctx)` call at `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/run_differs.py:237` **survives the entire reconciler suite — all 3,637 tests pass**. Only the live Jira DC lane catches it.

Measured 2026-08-28 while closing `seagreen-fortuitous-crayfish` (`f449-be6a-be56-4fef`), whose fix that call implements.

## Why this matters more than a missing test

The overlay this call feeds has genuine teeth: mutating its *behaviour* is killed by 5 tests, including an anchored clobber pair with a negative control. So the logic is well covered. What is uncovered is the **wiring** — whether the call is made at all. That asymmetry is the dangerous shape: a reader sees a well-tested module and reasonably concludes the feature is protected, when in fact deleting its single invocation is invisible to every offline test.

Concretely, `f449` fixed a live DC rich-text echo re-diffing against a stale JQL snapshot. If this call is ever dropped — by a refactor, a bad merge resolution, or an extraction moving code between modules — that bug returns silently and only a live-DC run reveals it. Several `src/rebar` modules are being split right now for module-size reasons, which is exactly the operation most likely to drop a call site.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An offline test fails when the `refresh_scoped_snapshot(ctx)` invocation is removed from `run_differs.py`.
- [ ] That test asserts the CALL HAPPENED (and with the right ctx), not merely that the downstream data looks refreshed — otherwise a coincidentally-fresh fixture satisfies it.
- [ ] The test does not require a live Jira DC instance or any CI-provider-specific trigger.
- [ ] Existing behaviour coverage is retained, not replaced: the 5 tests that kill the behaviour mutant must still kill it.

## Testing

- **Mutation-first, and this is the whole point:** seed the deletion, confirm the new test goes RED, restore, confirm GREEN. Verify the seed actually applied (a replace landing in a comment produces a mutant that was never seeded, which reads as a false kill).
- **Anchor against vacuity.** An assertion that the snapshot is fresh passes when the fixture was already fresh and the call never ran. Assert the invocation itself — spy/record the call — then separately assert its effect.
- Prefer an assertion that survives a rename or a module move (the call site is likely to be relocated by an ongoing split), or state plainly why a location-coupled assertion is acceptable here.

## Related

- `f449-be6a-be56-4fef` — the ticket whose fix this call implements; NOT closed, blocked on an AC3 provenance split.
- Separate small defect found alongside: the ADR citation "ADR 0037 s3" is WRONG in `f449`'s body and twice in `snapshot_lagfree_refresh.py`'s docstring. ADR 0037 is oss-contribution-intake-posture; the real support is `docs/adr/0055-jira-family-sub-seam.md:282`. Worth correcting in the same change since it is shipped source prose.
data.title: refresh_scoped_snapshot wiring has NO offline coverage: deleting the call survives the entire 3637-test reconciler suite
